task.title: Fix round 2: test strength of the first fixes (F-006, F-007, F-008, F-009)
task.description:
Four minor findings of review round 2 about the tests of round 1's fixes: 14 mutants of the fix code survive, so the behaviour they stand for is pinned by no assertion. Each finding is in `fix_context.review_feedback`; the full text is in findings.json and every mutant (file:line, anchor, replacement) in research-evidence/mutation-2.md. Task T22 has just changed the same production file (results/T22.result.json says what, and which lines of the quiet catalog re-read moved), so some anchors have moved. The task is done when every finish line below holds, the two test files and the type check pass, and nothing outside the owned files changed.

F-006. The bounds of `placeFiltersPopover` and the removal of its resize listener are unpinned: R2-2 (opens above although there is less room above), R2-4, R2-5, R2-6, R2-7 (the floors and the 420 px cap), R2-9 (the resize listener is never removed). F-007. The quiet catalog re-read is pinned by one same-snapshot fixture: R2-14 (a return while the first read is loading), R2-16 (a return after the snapshot changed), R2-17 and R2-19 (a later full read after a quiet one), R2-18 (the snapshot match in `graphState`), R2-26 (the freshness reason). F-008. The node-memory test asserts only that nothing is written, so deleting the effect that fills the memory (R2-23) stays green; nothing reaches, through Back, a node that exists only in that memory. F-009. Removing `visible={view === "metaproject"}` from App.tsx (R2-28) stays green, so the line the fixes of round 1's F-003 and F-004 hang on is pinned by no test.

Finish line: `scratch_check2.py mutants --ids R2-2,R2-4,R2-5,R2-6,R2-7,R2-9,R2-14,R2-16,R2-17,R2-18,R2-19,R2-23,R2-26 --tests src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx` and `--ids R2-28 --tests src/App.dom.test.tsx` report each mutant as killed. For a mutant the tool reports as invalid because T22 moved its anchor, your result names the line that now carries that behaviour and the test that pins it. For a mutant no DOM test can kill at a reasonable cost, it says why, and for R2-28 specifically the reviewer accepts as an alternative a statement that the wiring rests on the live check only; prefer a test if the composition can be rendered with the explorer stubbed. The F-008 test shows the memory working (Back to a node known only from a lookup shows its panel at once), not only that it is left alone. A test added here asserts what a user or a caller can observe — rendered text, roles, the requests the explorer sends, the style the popover gets, a callback's arguments — not the wording of the source. The production files are owned so that a test can be given a seam it needs; a change of behaviour in them is a `behavior_changes` entry, and a real defect a new test exposes is reported, with the test, before it is fixed. R2-12 and R2-30 also survive and are not in this task: the reviewer judged both redundant code with no input a test can drive.

Scope freeze: fix the findings named here and nothing else. Anything else you notice goes into `noticed_not_touched`; a choice the plan's state x event matrix does not decide goes into `behavior_changes` with `needs_operator: true` and its alternatives. A reviewer's `suggested_fix` is a hypothesis: reproduce the finding first, check the suggestion against the matrix, and say in `notes` where your fix diverged from it or where a finding did not reproduce. Existing tests are not weakened or deleted to make room for a fix. The fixes you are correcting were themselves reviewed as answers to findings, and the defects they brought were missed for that reason: for each change you make, name in `notes` who else reads the thing you changed (search for it) and what they now get.
